questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an attribute of a state?
questions.explanation: Many states are multilingual; the essential attributes are population, territory, government and sovereignty.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: Sovereignty means
options: the power of the courts to punish offenders
the size of a country's armed forces
the supreme authority of the state within its territory
the right of citizens to vote
questions.explanation: Sovereignty is final and absolute authority, internally and externally.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: A constitution is
options: a list of registered political parties
the body of rules by which a state is governed
questions.explanation: It establishes the organs of government and defines their powers and limits.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: A constitution whose provisions are contained in a single document is described as
questions.explanation: A written constitution is codified in one formal document.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: The constitution of Britain is best described as
questions.explanation: It rests on statutes, conventions and judicial decisions rather than one document.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: A rigid constitution is one which
options: can only be amended by a special procedure
can be amended by a simple majority
questions.explanation: Amendment typically requires a special majority and sometimes state approval.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: The doctrine of separation of powers was popularised by
questions.explanation: Montesquieu set it out in The Spirit of the Laws.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: The principle of checks and balances is designed to ensure that
options: no organ of government becomes too powerful
questions.explanation: Each organ restrains the others, for example by veto, confirmation or judicial review.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: The organ of government responsible for making laws is the
questions.explanation: The legislature enacts, amends and repeals the laws of the state.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: The organ of government that interprets the laws is the
questions.explanation: Courts apply and interpret the law in actual disputes.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: The organ of government that implements and enforces laws is the
questions.explanation: The executive carries the laws into effect through the machinery of administration.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: A bicameral legislature is one that consists of
questions.explanation: Two chambers allow a second look at legislation and represent different interests.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: The National Assembly of Nigeria consists of the
options: Senate and the Council of State
Senate and the House of Representatives
Federal Executive Council and the Senate
questions.explanation: Nigeria operates a bicameral federal legislature.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: How many members make up the Senate of the Federal Republic of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Three senators from each of the 36 states plus one for the Federal Capital Territory.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: The House of Representatives of Nigeria has
questions.explanation: Members are elected from 360 federal constituencies.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: A system of government in which powers are shared between a central government and component units is
questions.explanation: Each level derives its powers from the constitution, not from the other.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: In a unitary system of government,
options: powers are shared equally between two levels
all powers are concentrated in the central government
questions.explanation: Local authorities exercise only the powers the centre chooses to delegate.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: A major feature of a confederation is that
options: the component units retain their sovereignty
there is a single national army
questions.explanation: The centre is weak and depends on the member states, which may secede.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: A presidential system of government is characterised by
options: the fusion of the executive and the legislature
the separation of the executive from the legislature
a ceremonial head of state only
the absence of a written constitution
questions.explanation: The president is separately elected and is not a member of the legislature.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: In a parliamentary system of government, the head of government is the
questions.explanation: The prime minister leads the government while the head of state is often ceremonial.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: Delegated legislation refers to laws made
options: by the courts in deciding cases
directly by the electorate in a referendum
by a body other than the legislature under powers granted by it
questions.explanation: Ministers and agencies issue regulations under an enabling Act.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: The rule of law implies, among other things,
options: equality of all citizens before the law
the supremacy of the armed forces
the right of the president to make laws alone
questions.explanation: No one is above the law, and no one may be punished except by due process.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: The concept of the rule of law is particularly associated with
questions.explanation: Dicey expounded the doctrine in his writings on the English constitution.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: Judicial review is the power of the courts to
options: determine the constitutionality of laws and official acts
make new laws for the state
questions.explanation: Legislation or executive action inconsistent with the constitution can be declared void.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: Fundamental human rights are entrenched in which chapter of the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Chapter II contains the non-justiciable objectives; Chapter IV contains enforceable rights.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: Democracy is best described as government
questions.explanation: Authority derives from the consent of the governed, expressed through elections.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: Universal adult suffrage means that
options: all adult citizens have the right to vote
questions.explanation: The franchise is extended to all adults without regard to sex, wealth or literacy.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: The body responsible for conducting federal elections in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: INEC registers voters and parties and conducts federal and state elections.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: A one-party system is characterised by
options: the absence of legal opposition parties
questions.explanation: Only one party is permitted to contest and hold power.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: Pressure groups differ from political parties in that pressure groups
options: do not seek to capture political power
questions.explanation: They seek to influence policy rather than to form a government.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: Public opinion may be described as
options: the manifesto of a political party
the view of the ruling party alone
the views held by the majority of citizens on a public issue
a decision of the supreme court
questions.explanation: It is the prevailing sentiment of the politically relevant public.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: A major characteristic of the civil service is
options: tenure that ends with each government
questions.explanation: Civil servants serve whichever government is in power and remain in office across changes.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: Anonymity as a feature of the civil service means that civil servants
options: do not take public credit or blame for policies
questions.explanation: The minister answers publicly for the ministry, not the officials who advised them.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: The administrative head of the civil service of the federation in Nigeria is the
options: Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
questions.explanation: The Head of Service oversees the federal civil service as its most senior officer.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: In Nigeria's federal arrangement, local government is regarded as the
options: an agency of the National Assembly
questions.explanation: The federal, state and local governments form the three tiers.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: The amalgamation of the Northern and Southern Protectorates of Nigeria in 1914 was carried out by
questions.explanation: Lugard was Governor-General and became the first head of a united Nigeria.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 is remembered for introducing
questions.explanation: For the first time a limited number of Nigerians could elect members to the Legislative Council.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: The Richards Constitution of 1946 is best remembered for introducing
questions.explanation: It created Northern, Western and Eastern regional councils.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: The Macpherson Constitution of Nigeria came into effect in
questions.explanation: It followed wide consultation and expanded regional legislative powers.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: Nigeria formally became a federation under the
questions.explanation: The 1954 constitution established a federal structure with clear regional autonomy.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: Nigeria attained political independence on
questions.explanation: Independence was granted on 1 October 1960, with Nigeria remaining a dominion until 1963.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: Nigeria became a republic in
questions.explanation: In 1963 the British monarch ceased to be head of state and a president replaced the Governor-General.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: The first military coup in Nigeria took place in
questions.explanation: The coup of 15 January 1966 ended the First Republic.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: The Nigerian civil war was fought between
questions.explanation: It began in July 1967 and ended in January 1970.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: The Second Republic in Nigeria began in
questions.explanation: Military rule gave way to the Shagari administration on 1 October 1979.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: Nigeria returned to civil rule under the Fourth Republic in
questions.explanation: The handover took place on 29 May 1999.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) was established in
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Lagos was signed in May 1975.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: The headquarters of the African Union is located in
questions.explanation: The AU, like the former OAU, is headquartered in Addis Ababa.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: Which organ of the United Nations has primary responsibility for maintaining international peace and security?
questions.explanation: The Security Council may authorise sanctions and the use of force.
questions.subject: Government

questions.question: How many permanent members does the United Nations Security Council have?
questions.explanation: China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States, each with a veto.
questions.subject: Government
